subject: Food Science
title: What Is Food Processing
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is Food Processing.

hook.text: Cooking an egg is food processing. So is making cheese, canning soup, or milling flour.

buildup.text: Processing ranges from minimal (washing, cutting) to moderate (cooking, fermenting) to extensive (extruding, hydrogenating).

discovery.text: Without processing, 40% of global food would spoil before reaching consumers. Processing extends shelf life from days to years.

twist.text: Not all processing is harmful. Pasteurization saves lives. Fortification prevents deficiency.

climax.text: The NOVA system classifies food into 4 processing levels.

punchline.text: All cooking is processing. The degree matters. Minimal processing feeds the world.

quiz.question: What percentage of food would spoil without processing?
options: 40% of global food would spoil before reaching consumers
